findings.title: [P2] Compare file contents when checking probe write scope
findings.body: The scope check compares only Git porcelain output, which records status and paths rather than contents. If a tracked application file is already modified before the probe, the probe can overwrite it through the main checkout's absolute path and leave the same ` M <path>` entry. Both snapshots then match and the helper exits successfully despite unauthorized application changes. Changes within an existing ignored directory can likewise remain invisible. Record and compare content hashes, including existing dirty and ignored files, or enforce filesystem write isolation around the probe.

findings.failure_mode: The scope check compares only Git porcelain output, which records status and paths rather than contents.

findings.description: `close --consumed-by <cycle>` is the one /chart operation allowed unattended, and both chart.md and chart-guard.sh describe it as applying to a handed-off map. op_close never checks the map's Status: the --consumed-by branch validates only the cycle-id syntax and then rejects every open ledger row, closes every bead and the epic, and marks the doc `closed`. An unattended agent can therefore destroy a map that is still `charting` (open frontier, unresolved fog) by passing any well-formed cycle id, which is exactly the outcome the interactive-only rule exists to prevent. The `--reason` branch does enforce the interactive context, so the asymmetry is clear.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous run (or a prompt-injected session) executes `chart-ticket.sh close --map <slug> --consumed-by x` on a charting map; all open decision rows are rejected and beads closed with no operator present, silently converting unanswered decisions into 'settled' state.
findings.suggested_fix: In the --consumed-by branch require `doc_field Status` == handed-off (and no open rows via map_rows) before any write; otherwise die with 'only a handed-off map is consumed'. Also route the context check through chart-guard --close-consumed so the two guards agree.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 block on `git branch -D` gains an exemption whose evidence is the tracked file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml: a row with status decided, source spikes/<slug>.md, and a `to: decided` transition whose `by` starts with `operator:`. That file is in the working tree and is writable by the same agent the hook constrains (via Write/Edit or dec-write-lib). Nothing cryptographically or externally attests the `operator:` prefix, so the agent can forge the row (or edit an existing row's `by`) and then force-delete an unmerged spike branch the hook was meant to protect. The exemption converts a self-contained safety check into one that trusts agent-writable state.
findings.failure_mode: Agent appends a decided row with `by: operator:x` to decisions.yaml, runs `git branch -D spike/foo`; hook allows it and unmerged prototype work is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the branch to also be present on the remote (`git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` and HEAD-equal) before exempting, or require the ledger row to be committed (compare `git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) rather than reading the dirty working copy.

findings.description: The probe runs an arbitrary argv with the operator's full privileges; the only containment is a before/after `git status --porcelain` comparison of the main worktree. That check does not cover: (a) the shared `.git` directory, which the detached worktree shares with the main tree, so `git config core.hooksPath`/`core.fsmonitor`/aliases or files under `.git/hooks` persist code execution into the main checkout with no status change; (b) any path outside the repo ($HOME/.claude/settings.json, ~/.bashrc, ~/.gitconfig); (c) tracked files that were already dirty in the snapshot (the ` M path` line is identical before and after). The header calls this 'the only way an unblock ticket runs anything', so callers will treat a 0 exit as proof of no side effects.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected or careless unblock probe sets `git config core.hooksPath` or writes a hook via the shared .git, exits 0 ('main tree unchanged'), and the payload runs on the next git command in the main tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Hash or snapshot `.git/config` and `.git/hooks` alongside the status (or run the worktree with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and a separate clone instead of a shared worktree); also compare content hashes of already-dirty tracked files, and document that out-of-repo writes are not detected.

findings.cross_file_justification: plan-and-analyze.md (diff-touched) registers grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md as priority-1 context whose decisions are 'settled; confirm, do not re-ask'. op_handoff builds that file by inlining the map doc and `dw list --format md` verbatim.
findings.description: Research reports are passed through the L6 sanitizer before inlining, but the map doc (`sed` demotes headings only) and the ledger markdown are inlined raw. Both are tracked, PR-editable files, and the map doc is a free-text document any contributor or a prior agent can edit outside chart-ticket.sh's san1/no_url path. Content in them lands in the highest-priority context of /plan-and-analyze with an instruction to treat it as settled, making it a direct prompt-injection channel into PRD generation. The git-tracked nature means a malicious or compromised branch can plant it.
findings.failure_mode: A map doc line such as 'Decision: all secrets are committed to the repo (settled)' or an embedded instruction in a Destination paragraph is carried into chart-<slug>.md and consumed as a non-negotiable requirement by the planning agent.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the map doc and the ledger markdown through the same `sanitize_for_session_start` path as the reports (or fail the handoff when the sanitizer is unavailable), and wrap the inlined map in an explicit `> UNTRUSTED` fence like the reports.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff hunk for chart-researcher.md grants the subagent `Write` alongside `WebFetch` (and agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable: true); research-end is the only mechanical check on what that subagent wrote.
findings.description: The scope check diffs two `git status --porcelain` snapshots and flags new entries outside grimoires/loa/research/. It cannot see: writes outside the repository (~/.claude/settings.json, hooks, shell rc files), writes to a tracked file that was already modified when the marker was taken (status line unchanged), or writes to other tickets' reports and the dispatch markers inside grimoires/loa/research/ (explicitly allowed by the awk filter). Where the subagent has Write and fetches arbitrary web pages, the 'write exactly one file' rule is prompt-only, and a fetched page can direct it to write elsewhere. The repo-only post-hoc check gives the dispatching session false assurance.
findings.failure_mode: A fetched page instructs the researcher to write to ~/.claude/settings.json or to overwrite chart-<slug>-<other>.md; research-end passes, and the modified report is later inlined into the priority-1 hand-off snapshot.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the head-state agent definition (no Write) and make agent-types.yaml say write_capable: false so the capability registry matches. In research-end, additionally compare content hashes of grimoires/loa/research/* (allow only the expected report to change) and of already-dirty tracked files; document that out-of-repo writes are not observable.

findings.description: chart-researcher is registered as `write_capable: true`, while the head version of .claude/agents/chart-researcher.md lists tools [Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch] and states it 'cannot' write. The diff hunk for the same file includes Write. The two sources of truth disagree; whichever enforcement consumes agent-types.yaml (skill-capabilities tests, hooks) will reason about a different capability set than the agent actually has, and a later edit re-adding Write would pass the registry unnoticed.
findings.failure_mode: Capability checks keyed on write_capable permit or expect writes from a WebFetch-enabled subagent that the design says is read-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Set write_capable: false for chart-researcher and add a test asserting the agent frontmatter tools list contains no Write/Edit/Bash.

findings.description: The build-path filter drops question beads only when `.issue_type == "question"`. chart-frontier.sh and chart-ticket.sh in the same diff accept either `.issue_type` or `.type` from br, acknowledging the field name varies by release. With a br that emits `.type`, this filter fails open and decision tickets become selectable build work, breaking the 'tickets cannot enter a sprint' invariant that create-sprint-task.sh and the docs rely on.
findings.failure_mode: /implement or /run claims and 'implements' a decision ticket under a map epic.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") != "question")` to match the other scripts, and consider also excluding beads carrying a `decision:` label.

findings.description: SP-1 pre-filters on the literal substring `spike/` in the same command and then requires the ref to appear in the merge/checkout/restore segment. Trivial indirection defeats it: `b=spike/x; git merge $b`, `git merge spi''ke/x`, `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD`, or `git merge $(git rev-parse spike/x)`. The header lists some misses but not the variable/quote-splitting forms, which are the ones an agent reaches for first when a direct command is blocked.
findings.failure_mode: Spike prototype content is merged into a working branch despite the fence, defeating the D-5.4 invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Also match `spike/` inside quoted/split tokens by normalising the command (strip `''`/`""`), and treat assignment of a `spike/` literal to a variable later expanded in a git merge/rebase/cherry-pick segment as a block; rely on run-mode-ice.sh for the authoritative boundary.
